chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, who said: Some of our companions informed me, from ʿĪṣ, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, from his father عليه السلام, who said:
“When the deceased dies, then proceed with his preparation and hasten him. And when the deceased dies while in a state of janābah, he is given one ghusl, then after that he is washed.”

So there is no contradiction between these reports and what we presented earlier, because the basis of all these narrations is ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim, and he is only one person. It is not permissible for a large group to be opposed by a single individual, as we have explained elsewhere. Even if it were sound, it could be understood as referring to a kind of recommendation rather than obligation and requirement. Moreover, it is possible that the intended meaning in these reports is that the command for ghusl after washing the deceased with the ghusl of janābah was actually directed to the one washing him, as though it had been said to him: you should wash the deceased with the ghusl of janābah and then you yourself should perform ghusl. Thus this may be an error from the narrator or the copyist. And this very narrator has narrated what we mentioned.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommended practice rather than binding obligation
key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the deceased person whose funeral preparation and washing are being discussed
key_terms.جَهَازِهِ: his funeral preparation and arrangements before burial
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: in a state of janābah requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: How should a deceased person who died in a state of janābah be washed according to this hadith in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This report addresses the prompt preparation of the deceased and the ruling concerning a deceased person who died in a state of janābah. The accompanying discussion weighs the report against other narrations, arguing that it does not overturn stronger transmitted evidence and may be understood as recommendation or as referring to the washer rather than the deceased.
